description:
FILED s445 (Fable, round-5 review of agent M). Probe: package Q4; sub new {bless {},shift} package main; my @r = Q4->import; print scalar(@r),","; my @s = Q4->new->unimport; print scalar(@s),"\n" -- perl 0,0; PCL 1,1 (measured on main c74e11f AND on the s446m tree; the SUPER:: spelling via %pcl-super-fallback diverges identically, probe fable-r5m-13.pl: perl isa-arm:0;bare-arm:0, PCL 1;1). The arms test (eq *wantarray* t) and return an empty p-flatten-marker in list context, else nil -- but a my-LIST assignment reaches them with *wantarray* NOT t, so they return nil = one undef element. NOT the SUPER path binding: a REAL parent method reached via SUPER:: sees wantarray==list and my @r = ... gives 0 (probe fable-r5m-12.pl) -- so the context protocol works for p-sub returns; what mis-reads it is the builtin arm inside p-method-call/p-super-call. Suspect: the emitted call site binds *wantarray* around the METHOD CALL differently from what the arm tests, or the marker path is fine and the t-test is reached under a nested bind. DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (cheap): instrument one arm to print *wantarray*, run the fable-r5m-14 probe -- says which of the two. Fix ONE shared helper for all four arms (rule 11); also note perl 5.39+ warns "Attempt to call undefined import method with arguments" when args are passed -- PCL prints nothing (documented warnings-gated class, not this task). Probes in scratchpad fable-r5m-7/11/13/14.pl.

=== DONE s448p (Opus agent P), commit 792a5e8 ===

THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (the one this task asked for) WAS TAKEN FIRST and
KILLED BOTH SUSPECTS: all four arms were instrumented to print *wantarray*, and
the reproducer prints `ARM-PROBE wa=t` at every list-context call site (`wa=nil`
only for the genuinely scalar one).  The context read was never wrong -- the
emitted site is `(p-array-= @r (p-list-ctx (p-method-call "Q4" "import")))` and
p-list-ctx is a MACRO binding *wantarray* to t around the call.

THE REAL CAUSE is the VALUE.  A p-flatten-marker is recognised only by the
argument-SPREADING walkers (p-push-impl, p-unshift, p-flatten-args,
%p-collect-list, %p-array-fill-item).  Every OTHER list consumer reaches its
scalar arm -- p-array-fill's `(t (when src (%p-array-store-scalar ...)))` for a
bare struct -- so the marker was stored as ONE element.

The family is WIDER than the task's two rows (all measured vs perl 5.40.3):
  my @r = Foo->import          perl 0   PCL 1
  my ($p) = Foo->import        perl undef  PCL defined
  for (Foo->import) {}         perl 0 iterations  PCL 1
  my %h = (Foo->import)        perl 0 keys  PCL 1
  join(",", Foo->import)       perl ""  PCL "#S(p-flatten-marker :array #())"
  print Foo->import            perl ""  PCL "#S(p-flatten-marker :array #())"
  sub r { return Foo->import } my @g = r()   perl 0  PCL 1
and the ones that were already right and stay right: push, `(Foo->import, "z")`,
`(Foo->import) x 2`, scalar context, `my $v = Foo->import`.

FIX: ONE shared helper %pcl-no-op-import-result (rule 11) called by all four
arms, returning an empty adjustable VECTOR in list context and nil otherwise --
the value `sub { return () }` already yields, which spreads correctly in the
walkers AND in every other consumer.  Two stale comments describing the marker
representation updated in the same commit.

perl 5.39+'s "Attempt to call undefined import method with arguments" warning
stays absent: documented warnings-gated class (#221), out of scope per the task.

GUARD: Pl/t/method-dispatch-01.t 6 -> 8 rows (2.7 s), both failing on the base
runtime (inverse-run).  Runtime-only, no emission change, so no generation bump.
The merge review owes the full sweep and the op/ companion leg (the `cl/**` row).
title: import/unimport NO-OP arms return UNDEF in list context: my @r = Foo->import gives 1 element (perl 0) -- all four arms (p-method-call x3 + %pcl-super-fallback), pre-existing
